cohort: 2305 women with epilepsy (44 with twin pregnancies and 2261 with singleton pregnancies) from the Raoul Wallenberg Australian Register of Antiepileptic Drugs in Pregnancy.
finding: While there was no significant difference in antiepileptic drug therapy between the groups, twin pregnancies in women with epilepsy were associated with older maternal age, increased use of assisted fertilization techniques, lower birth weight, and a higher risk of fetal malformations and seizures in infancy.
mod_finding: Babies from twin pregnancies were more often delivered by cesarean section compared to singleton pregnancies.
